news.title: From $6 eggs to $50,000 cars, these charts show how inflation has defined the past 5 years
news.description: Rising prices have been crushing consumer confidence and biting at Americans’ wallets for more than five years now.
news.author: Genna Contino

copy.hook: Eggs hit $6. Did your paycheck grow that fast?
copy.explain: Inflation means prices rising across the economy. Over five years it pushed eggs to $6 and new cars past $50,000, so each dollar buys less than it used to. That squeeze is why consumer confidence, meaning how upbeat shoppers feel, has stayed low.
copy.takeaway: If prices rise faster than your money grows, you are quietly getting poorer.
copy.question: Which price jump from the last 5 years hit you hardest: eggs, cars, or rent?
